name: Clifford+T scalar rule (E)
summary: A π/4 Z-spider connected to a −π/4 X-spider is the empty diagram (the scalar 1).
description:
The scalar diagram consisting of a Z-spider with phase $\frac\pi4$ connected to an X-spider with phase $-\frac\pi4$ represents the number $1$, so it is equal to the empty diagram.

Jeandel, Perdrix, Vilmart and Wang showed that this equation cannot be derived from the earlier rules of the ZX-calculus, using a simple invariant (the parity of the number of odd-degree X-spiders plus the number of Hadamards). As it only involves angles that are multiples of $\pi/4$, this was another proof that the Clifford+T fragment was incomplete. Adding (E) made the older scalar rules (IV) and (ZO) derivable, and it is an axiom of all the Jeandel–Perdrix–Vilmart complete axiomatisations and of Vilmart's near-minimal one.
